## Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2t(t-1)}$

This is derived from an upper bound via a Steiner-system argument. I did not verify that the bound is attained, so the value rests on the assumption that a matching construction exists along $n_e = t^{2e-1}$.

**Setup.** In a $K_{2,t+1}$-free graph, every pair of vertices has at most $t$ common neighbours. For a $t$-set $B$, let $S_B$ be the set of vertices adjacent to all of $B$.

**Step 1: $|S_B| \le t$ whenever $|S_B| \ge t$.** If $|S_B| \ge t+1$, any two vertices of $B$ would have at least $t+1$ common neighbours (all of $S_B$), contradicting $K_{2,t+1}$-freeness. So every nonempty $S_B$ of size at least $t$ has size exactly $t$.

**Step 2: the blocks are linear.** Call a $t$-set $A$ a block if $|S_B|=t$ for the corresponding $B$ (equivalently, $A$ is a side of some $K_{t,t}$). If two blocks $S_B$ and $S_{B'}$ both contain a pair $\{v,w\}$, then $B, B' \subseteq N(v)\cap N(w)$. Since $|N(v)\cap N(w)| \le t$ and $|B|=|B'|=t$, we get $B=B'$. So distinct blocks share at most one vertex.

**Step 3: counting.** Linearity gives $\#\text{blocks}\cdot\binom{t}{2} \le \binom{n}{2}$, so
$$\#\text{blocks} \le \frac{n(n-1)}{t(t-1)}.$$
Each $K_{t,t}$ with sides $A$ and $B$ yields two blocks, $A$ and $B$. A given $t$-set $A$ lies on at most one $K_{t,t}$, since its common neighbourhood has size at most $t$ and must equal the other side. Hence each copy uses two distinct blocks and each block is used at most once, so
$$ex(n, K_{t,t}, K_{2,t+1}) \le \frac{n(n-1)}{2t(t-1)}.$$

**Step 4: the limit.** Dividing by $n^2$ and letting $e\to\infty$ gives an upper bound of $\frac{1}{2t(t-1)}$ on the limit. Matching this requires a near-perfect Steiner system $S(2,t,n)$ (for instance, from affine geometry over $\mathbb{F}_t$) whose blocks can be paired into $K_{t,t}$'s consistently with the $K_{2,t+1}$-free condition. I have not verified that construction, and the odd exponent $2e-1$ presumably comes from it.

ANSWER: $\frac{1}{2t(t-1)}$
